Read-only research task in the git repo at /home/user/fortress (branch claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr — the "first ascent" record of the Fortress revival). Do NOT modify anything, do NOT touch the worktree /home/user/fortress-clean (another agent is running builds there — avoid running anything expensive; this is a documentation/git-history dig only).

QUESTION: What did the test suites actually cost in wall-clock time across the first ascent, especially `ant testSystem`? The user (Pavol) recalls testSystem taking around 25 minutes at some point, but the recent clean-ladder record shows testSystem at 3m08s BEFORE the parallelization speedup and ~2m30s after. Either the 25-min memory refers to a different configuration/suite/era, or times improved dramatically along the way. Find the evidence.

WHERE TO LOOK (search breadth: very thorough):
1. `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md` — the original 2026-08 baseline writeup. Extract every wall-clock timing it records for testFast/testSystem/compileAll, and the environment context (JDK, machine/container, sequential vs parallel, cache state).
2. `explorations/test-suite-speedup.md` — the speedup design/measurement doc. Extract before/after timings and what specifically was changed (cache wipe, parallel tracks, sharding), plus any intermediate measurements.
3. `explorations/modernization-plan.md` — gate timing records per rung, if any.
4. Git history of the working branch: `git log --oneline` and commit messages that mention timings (grep the log for patterns like `testSystem`, `min`, `[0-9]m[0-9]`, `12m`, `25m`, etc. — e.g. `git log --format='%H %s' | ...` then `git show -s --format=%B <sha>` on hits). The gate numbers are usually recorded in commit message bodies. Include the speedup commits `4b1e500ca` and `e0f550094` and the baseline-era commits.
5. Any other explorations/*.md with timing mentions (grep for "testSystem", "wall", "minutes", timing patterns across explorations/).

ANALYZE: Build a small timeline: era/rung → testFast time → testSystem time → environment notes (JDK, sequential/parallel, first-run-vs-cached, single suite target vs testAll/testCompiler etc.). Specifically hunt for anything near 25 minutes: was there a ~25-min testSystem run early on (e.g. cold caches, slower container, pre-speedup sequential run, or a different target like the full `ant test`/testAll/testCompiler that bundles more)? Distinguish `ant testFast` vs `ant testSystem` vs any combined targets carefully — the 25-min memory might be testFast (which WAS ~13 min post-baseline, but check whether it was ever ~25 min earlier, e.g. before some fix) or a combined run (testFast+testSystem+compile ≈ 17 min) or a genuinely slower testSystem in the early baseline sessions.

REPORT: A concise timeline table of every dated/attributable timing found (with source: file+line or commit SHA), then your best-evidence answer to (a) what made testSystem as fast as ~3 min even before the speedup, i.e. was it ever much slower and why, and (b) what the ~25-min memory most plausibly refers to. Quote the exact sentences/numbers you rely on with their sources. Raw data only — no file dumps.

1	# Test-suite baseline on JDK 8 (2026-08-18)
2	
3	First run of the 2012 test suite on the grafted tree (trunk `a874948` +
4	pluckyporcupine migration + build patches; branch tip `b598e0e`).
5	Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 container, OpenJDK 8u482, ant 1.10.14, Scala 2.10.7
6	(vendored). Commands: `ant testFast`, `ant testSystem`.
7	
8	## Results
9	
10	| suite | scope | result |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| `ant testFast` | 48 JUnit suites: unit tests + **CompilerJUTest (642)** + OtherCompilerJUTest (263) + LibraryJUTest (55) + ParserJUTest (188) | **all pass** (≈1,400 tests, 0 failures, ~12 min) |
13	| `ant testSystem` | 382 interpreter system tests (`ProjectFortress/tests/*.test`) | **375 pass, 7 fail** (~2 min) |
14	
15	Not yet run: `testNotPassing` (expected-failing), `testDemos`, `testsyntax`,
16	`testCruiseControl`/nightly variants.
17	
18	## The 7 interpreter failures — both causes understood
19	
20	**6 × `System` api shadowing** (`ParamRef`, `WordCountSmall`, `setMakerTest0`,
21	`LongStringTests`, `CovCollTest`, `FileConversion` — symptom:
22	`FortressBuiltin.JavaString/StringVector is undefined`):
23	the interpreter's original `Library/System.fsi` declares
24	`args : ImmutableArray[\String,ZZ32\]`, but David Chase's 2012-07-19 import
25	(`5a68404`) added a minimal, compiler-oriented
26	`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/System.fsi` (getProperty only), and
27	LibraryBuiltin shadows Library for the interpreter. **Pre-existing on the 2012
28	trunk, not a graft regression** — Chase's own merge commit `575fe64`
29	(2012-07-19) says: "merged, failing some tests that I think are irrelevant (at
30	least under 1.7)". pluckyporcupine's June-12 base predates the shadowing file,
31	so their tree passes these — at the cost of lacking the July compiler work.
32	Candidate fix: extend `LibraryBuiltin/System.fsi/fss` to cover the original
33	api surface (`args`, `programName`, ...).
34	
35	**1 × `realArith`** — float-printing last digit:
36	`a Float: 2.718281828459045 =/= a FloatLiteral: 2.7182818284590455`.
37	JDK-era artifact (double parse/print behavior differs from the 2012 JDK 6/7
38	toolchain); harmless but should be understood before the JDK 11 rung.
39	
40	## Major discovery: the bytecode compiler path WORKS on JDK 8
41	
42	pluckyporcupine's README says "The compiler works, but running compiled
43	programs does not." **On JDK 8 that is false.** Verified end-to-end:
44	
45	```bash
46	cd ProjectFortress
47	../bin/fortress compile LibraryBuiltin/System.fss      # native-backed lib deps
48	../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss  # must be compiled once
49	../bin/fortress compile hello.fss
50	../bin/fortress run hello one two three
51	# fortress.home is  /home/user/fortress
52	# Hello, World!
53	# one
54	# three
55	# two        <- out of order: Fortress `for` loops are implicitly PARALLEL
56	```
57	
58	All 642 `CompilerJUTest` tests (including the 52 `.test` files that compile
59	*and execute* programs via `bin/run`) pass.
60	
61	Two traps that produced the historical "compiler is broken" verdict:
62	
63	1. **Stale caches.** With leftover state in `default_repository/caches/`,
64	   compiled programs die with
65	   `NoSuchMethodError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println(...)` — byte-for-byte
66	   pluckyporcupine's NOTES.md error (they saw it on Java 9; we reproduced it
67	   on JDK 8 before wiping caches). Fresh caches (`rm -rf
68	   default_repository/caches/*`, then recompile; the JUnit harness does
69	   `Shell.resetRepository()`) make it vanish. Their failure was plausibly
70	   this, not Java 9.
71	2. **Imported library components are not auto-compiled.** A program importing
72	   `System` / `CompilerSystem` needs those compiled into the bytecode cache
73	   first (errors: `Resource not found: System.class`,
74	   `NoClassDefFoundError: CompilerSystem$args`).
75	
76	Remaining truth in the old caveat: `hello.fss` still cannot run on the
77	*interpreter* (its imports resolve into the compiler-path library surface),
78	and the compiler still rejects constructs the 2012 team hadn't finished
79	(e.g. pluckyporcupine hit "mutable bindings not yet handled" on other
80	programs). The compiler is *incomplete*, not *broken*.
81	
82	## Postscript (2026-08-19): all failures fixed
83	
84	Both failure classes were fixed the next day — the suite is now fully green:
85	
86	- The six `System`-shadowing failures: `LibraryBuiltin/System.fsi/fss`
87	  deleted, compiler `getProperty` moved into `CompilerSystem` where `args`
88	  already lived, `hello.fss` imports updated (commit "Fix System api
89	  shadowing"). **The compile recipe above changed accordingly**: there is no
90	  `LibraryBuiltin/System.fss` anymore; compile the library chain in order —
91	  `LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss`, `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`,
92	  `../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`, `../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss`,
93	  `../Library/CompilerSystem.fss` — then the program. See
94	  `repo-internals.md` for why the order matters.
95	- `realArith`: the `e` constant in `Library/Constants.fss` was hand-tuned to
96	  the 2012 JDK's `exp(1.0)` (1 ulp above correctly-rounded e); corrected to
97	  the double nearest e (commit "Correct the e constant").
98	
99	## Baseline verdict
100	
101	The grafted tree is healthier than either parent lineage: it carries the full
102	Aug-2012 feature state, compiles under JDK 8, passes the entire unit/compiler
103	suite, and 98% of the interpreter suite, with all 7 failures explained (6
104	pre-existing upstream, 1 JDK-era cosmetic).
105

1	# Test-suite speedup: investigation and proposal (2026-08-21)
2	
3	Status: **intervention 1 implemented and gated green** (see "Results"
4	at the end); interventions 2–4 remain proposals. Baseline: `ant testFast`
5	≈ 11 min, `ant testSystem` ≈ 2 min, on 4 CPUs.
6	
7	## Where the time goes
8	
9	testFast's ~11 min is 97% three serial JUnit suites: CompilerJUTest
10	(642 tests, 256 s), LibraryJUTest (55 tests, 201 s), OtherCompilerJUTest
11	(263 tests, 164 s). Per-command aggregate across the whole run: **link
12	376 s** (221 links), compile 118 s, subprocess `run` 92 s (223 child JVM
13	launches, but only ~200 ms fixed overhead each — the work is real),
14	typecheck 8 s. Ant's default `forkmode=perTest` forks one JVM per suite
15	class; that overhead is negligible (~5% of wall).
16	
17	**The single biggest cost is the duplicated cold-cache library rebuild.**
18	`CompilerJUTest` and `LibraryJUTest` each call `Shell.resetRepository()`
19	in `suite()` (CompilerJUTest.java:31, LibraryJUTest.java:31), wiping the
20	shared cache; each then pays a cold first link — 99.4 s and 120.3 s
21	respectively — versus a ≤ 19.7 s warm-cache worst case in
22	OtherCompilerJUTest (which doesn't reset). The two cold rebuilds are
23	~220 s of the 620 s the big suites consume. The reset's documented
24	rationale (repo-internals.md: fresh-cache compile-order trap) protects
25	against a *stale* cache, not a *warm* one — and GraphRepository's
26	timestamp-based staleness checking (GraphRepository.java:483–659)
27	validates a retained cache anyway.
28	
29	testSystem: 382 in-process interpreter tests, flat distribution (mean
30	350 ms, max 12.7 s), no cache wipe, no subprocesses.
31	
32	## Ranked interventions
33	
34	1. **Skip the second cache wipe** (~120 s saved, low risk). Gate the
35	   `resetRepository()` calls on a property (e.g. `fortress.junit.reset`,
36	   default true) so testFast wipes once up front and LibraryJUTest
37	   inherits CompilerJUTest's warm cache; or simply drop LibraryJUTest's
38	   reset. Validate: two back-to-back testFast runs, diff pass/fail sets.
39	2. **Run the three big suites concurrently** (up to ~2× on the 620 s
40	   block, medium risk). Ant 1.10's `<junit threads="3">` works with the
41	   current effective forkmode — but is UNSAFE without cache isolation
42	   (mid-run wipes + no locking anywhere in the cache layer;
43	   Linker.java:97–104 writes jars with no temp+rename). Isolation route:
44	   per-suite FORTRESS_HOME trees with hardlink-copied caches (cache is
45	   only 53 MB, `cp -al` is instant).
46	3. **Shard testSystem** (~120 s → ~40–60 s, low risk). SystemJUTest takes
47	   `-Dtests=<dir>` (SystemJUTest.java:33) and neither wipes nor spawns —
48	   plain `-Dfortress.caches=<shard>` isolation suffices. Set
49	   `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` per shard (the interpreter already runs its own
50	   ForkJoin pool at availableProcessors/2; Driver.java:518–530).
51	4. **Enabling fixes** (each small, independently correct):
52	   - `bin/run_classpath:25` (and `bin/runOpt:32`,
53	     `BytecodeOptimizeEverything.sh:17`) hardcode
54	     `default_repository/caches/...` — child `run` JVMs ignore any cache
55	     redirection. Honor `FORTRESS_CACHES`.
56	   - `Shell.resetRepository()` (Shell.java:119) wipes
57	     `REPOSITORY + "/caches"` instead of `ProjectProperties.CACHES` — a
58	     latent bug: a redirected suite still destroys the shared cache, and
59	     the wipe also deletes the git-tracked `caches/global.map`.
60	
61	## Dead ends (measured/verified, don't revisit)
62	
63	- **In-JVM threading of tests**: blocked by FileTests' global
64	  System.out/err swap (pass/fail is decided by scanning the captured
65	  stream, FileTests.java:301–306), Shell's process-wide mode flags,
66	  static-final cache singletons (ProjectProperties.java:283–297), and
67	  Driver's static interpreter state.
68	- **Eliminating the 223 `bin/fortress run` subprocesses**: forbidden by
69	  design — InstantiatingClassloader throws "Second classloader
70	  detected!!" on a second instance per JVM — and the ceiling is only
71	  ~45 s anyway.
72	- **`forkmode="once"`**: a pessimization (fork overhead is negligible;
73	  suite JVM sharing would leak mode-flag statics).
74	
75	Helpful knobs that already exist: `fortress.unittests.seed` (reproducible
76	shuffle), `fortress.unittests.count` (stop after N — quick smoke runs),
77	`-Dtests=<dir>` on SystemJUTest, `fortress.junit.verbose`. Tests are
78	order-independent by design (reshuffled every run); no junit timeouts
79	anywhere, so parallel load can't cause spurious timeout failures.
80	
81	## Suggested sequencing
82	
83	(1) alone is a one-property change worth ~2 min of every gate. (4)'s two
84	fixes are prerequisites for (2)/(3) and are correct on their own. Combined
85	ceiling on 4 CPUs: gate ≈ 13 min → ≈ 5–6 min. All of this also folds into
86	the clean-ladder rebuild (the enabling fixes belong in the base block).
87	
88	## Results: intervention 1 (implemented 2026-08-21)
89	
90	Shape: `CompilerJUTest`/`LibraryJUTest` gate their `suite()` reset on
91	`fortress.junit.reset` (default true — standalone runs unchanged);
92	`testFast` in build.xml does one up-front file-only wipe of
93	`default_repository/caches` (same semantics as `Shell.resetRepository`:
94	files deleted, directories kept) and passes
95	`-Dfortress.junit.reset=false` to the forked suites.
96	
97	Validation, JDK 25, 4 CPUs: two back-to-back `ant testFast` runs plus
98	`ant testSystem`, all fully green (47 suites, 1,377 tests, 0 failures ×2;
99	382/0/0). LibraryJUTest's link phase inherits CompilerJUTest's warm
100	cache: 201 s → 88 s. Wall clock: testFast 11 min → **8 min 53 s** (both
101	runs within 1 s of each other, so warm-vs-cold start of the whole target
102	does not matter — the up-front wipe restores identical conditions).
103	`git status` after a run is clean: the suites rewrite
104	`caches/global.map` byte-identically, as before.
105	
106	## Results: interventions 2–4 (implemented 2026-08-21)
107	
108	Shape:
109	
110	- **Enabling fixes (4)**: every place that hardcoded
111	  `default_repository/caches` on the classpath or in reset logic now
112	  honors the redirection: `bin/fortress_classpath`, `bin/run_classpath`,
113	  `bin/runOpt`, `bin/BytecodeOptimizeEverything.sh` derive
114	  `CACHES="${FORTRESS_CACHES:-$FORTRESS_HOME/default_repository/caches}"`;
115	  `Shell.resetRepository` wipes `ProjectProperties.CACHES` instead of the
116	  hardwired repository path. In-JVM cache paths already followed
117	  `fortress.caches`/`FORTRESS_CACHES` via ProjectProperties (which
118	  auto-creates the subdirectories on class init), so no other Java
119	  changes were needed. Still hardcoded, deliberately out of scope
120	  (unused by the suite): `fortress.bat`, `bin/debugOpt`,
121	  `bin/runOptCollect`, `bin/BytecodeOptimizeCompilerTests`, the nine
122	  `bin/comp/*` scripts, and `Inlining.java:308/310`.
123	- **Parallel testFast (2)**: a `fastTrack` macrodef forks each junit
124	  track with its own private cache tree
125	  (`ProjectFortress/test-caches/fast-<id>`, gitignored) via the
126	  `fortress.caches` sysproperty + `FORTRESS_CACHES` env (the env var is
127	  inherited by the `bin/fortress` child processes ShellTest/TestTest
128	  spawn). Four tracks run under `<parallel>`: the three big suites
129	  (CompilerJUTest, LibraryJUTest, OtherCompilerJUTest) plus one track
130	  with every remaining small suite. Per-track junit-report dirs avoid
131	  formatter collisions; `errorProperty`/`failureProperty` converge on one
132	  `<fail>` after the barrier (ant properties are write-once and
133	  project-global, so parallel sets are race-free).
134	- **Sharded testSystem (3)**: `FileTests.interpreterSuite` gained an
135	  optional `-Dfortress.suite.shard=i/n` filter (sort names, keep
136	  `index % n == i`; inactive by default). testSystem runs four shards
137	  under `<parallel>`, each with a private cache tree and
138	  `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` so four interpreter runtimes don't fight over
139	  cores.
140	
141	Validation, JDK 25, 4 CPUs, fresh `ant compileAll`: both targets fully
142	green — testFast 0 failures across all four tracks, testSystem
143	382/0/0 (shards 95+95+97+95).
144	
145	Measured wall clock:
146	
147	- **testFast: 8 min 53 s → 5 min 23 s** (user time 17 min 39 s — ~3.3×
148	  CPU utilization). Track times: compiler 642 tests / 300 s, library
149	  55 / 243 s (cold again — the warm-cache handoff from intervention 1 is
150	  gone since tracks are isolated, yet the overlap more than pays for
151	  it), othercompiler 263 / 321 s (longest track — sets the wall), misc
152	  ~45 suites / ~40 s. Ceiling: further gains need splitting
153	  OtherCompilerJUTest itself.
154	- **testSystem: 2 min 8 s — wall-neutral** vs the ~2 min single run.
155	  Honest result: the interpreter's work-stealing runtime already
156	  saturated 4 CPUs in the single-JVM run (~404 s user either way);
157	  sharding just trades runtime-level for process-level parallelism.
158	  Kept anyway for the isolation win below.
159	
160	Combined gate: ~13 min (pre-intervention-1) → **~7.5 min**.
161	
162	Isolation win, independent of speed: neither target touches
163	`default_repository/caches` at all any more — the old testFast pre-wipe
164	of `cache0` is gone, both targets build in `ProjectFortress/test-caches`
165	(deleted at target start) — so test runs can no longer dirty the tracked
166	`caches/global.map` or invalidate a developer's warm interpreter cache.
167	(`ant compileAll` still wipes `cache0` via the pre-existing `cleanCache`
168	over-wipe; known separate issue.) The two targets share the same
169	`test-caches` root, so they must run sequentially, as before.
